patch.value: GH-782: guide-shell special-cases one multi-word command name and duplicates its status derivation, and calendar's throw-only validation call is unexplained, inside package-managed built-ins consumers cannot patch

GH-782.

Three runtime-maintainability gaps in the managed calendar and guide-shell built-ins, reported against published 2026.7.27. They are individually small, but the files are package-managed, so a downstream repository cannot sustainably patch them and each one is a latent behaviour-drift site.

Reported findings:

- guide-shell maps update-many to update_many with a one-command special case. Registry lookup should normalize every multi-word command name consistently, for example by translating hyphens and whitespace to underscores, before falling back to an empty definition. As written, the second multi-word command to arrive silently resolves to an empty definition instead of its registry entry, and the failure is a missing capability rather than an error.
- guide-shell derives the filtered, locale-sorted status-ID list twice, once during initialization and once during completion-status execution. Two copies of one derivation is the standard precondition for the two diverging under later edits.
- calendar calls resolveCalendarOutputFormat standalone purely so that it throws on an invalid format before runCalendar, but nothing records that the call is throw-only, so it reads as a dead result and invites removal.

The unifying point is that a special case, a duplicated derivation and an unexplained throw-only call are each a place where the next edit can change behaviour without any gate noticing, inside artifacts that consumers cannot repair.

guide-shell normalizes every multi-word command name through one generic rule rather than a per-command special case, covered by a test that adds a second multi-word command; The filtered locale-sorted status-ID derivation exists once in guide-shell and both call sites use it; The throw-only purpose of the standalone resolveCalendarOutputFormat call in calendar is recorded so the call cannot be removed as dead code; GH-782 is closed with evidence that the normalizer handles a command name it was not written for
